text: The tea infuser is great. Only major complain is that the coffee strainer doesn't fit well in regular 10 oz. mugs. The bottom of the strainer sits in the coffee and never completely drains because of this.

I was extremely excited to try this, especially when I found it for less than $1! When it arrived, I was impressed with its durability and smart design. It looks big in person, but it still works perfectly with my Keurig and fits well on all the different mugs I have used to brew with it. I like it so well, I am thinking of getting a few more for gifts!

My husband and I switched to an iCoffee after having a Keurig and found we could not use our reusable Keurig K-Cups with our new iCoffee. I was having a difficult time finding a reusable K-Cup that would work with our iCoffee and stumbled across these during the process. Both my husband and I enjoy coffee and tea on a regular basis and have rather large coffee cups, so, I was a little concerned that these would be too small but they fit perfectly on all of our cups.

As for the taste and usage, there is a little splatter when using with the iCoffee that is easily cleaned and honestly hardly noticed. I love the way the coffee and tea taste with these. Our old reusable K-Cups always left a funny taste and could only be filled with about 1 tablespoon of grounds or tea leaves. These however, can hold plenty of grounds for a strong cup of coffee or tea. Another thing I would like to point out is even though this product wouldn't be necessary for someone using a tea bag, they are quite useful for someone who enjoys using loose leaf tea and either has to make several cups or does not have a steeper. Again, using our old reusable K-Cup, tea never tasted quite right.
This product works well, and cleans up easily.
makes an excellent cup of coffee

The filters are very well constructed. I used the small one for a cup of coffee and I need to leave the filter about 4-5 minutes for the strength I like.

The Java Concepts Reusable Pour-Over Filter Pod is basically a drip coffee maker. Drip coffee is made by pouring water, preferably hot water, over ground roasted coffee beans. Using this compact device in conjunction with the hot water output of a Keurig style coffee maker is a convenient way to make a single cup of coffee at a fraction of the cost of a single brew pod. A weaker or stronger brew is easy to accomplish by simply adjusting the amount of grounds used.
I have used mine everyday since it came and is a welcome addition to my coffee making arsenal. Yes, I use the included drip tray. Clean up is a snap and the sturdy construction means that it will stand up to repeated hard use.
great to use with kcup machine
Does not come with mug. Change the image please. It's misguided.

I've been using one of these for about 10 weeks and really like it. Best filter I've found so far. Seems to be quite sturdy. It cleans up real easy. Just put some newspaper on the counter, turn the filter over, and give it a good rap on the paper. Most of the grounds come out and just rinse under the faucet to get rid of the rest. I then take a paper towel and finish cleaning it.
But it does leave some sludge in your coffee, if that bothers you. .
Ordered the Java Concepts hoping for the end to having to use paper filters. Unfortunately, too many grounds go through this to really be considered a good replacement. Back to hoping...
Oh so easy...add grounds pour in hot water .....brewed coffee...single or caraffe

Would not recommend. The pores on these filters are not good for coffee. They make very silty coffee...much more than a french press. I would just get the 3 cup Bodum french press. It fits perfectly under a Keurig for easy, but good coffee.

This. is. AWESOME.
This turned my Keurig brewer into a super-fast single-serve pour-over system. I just got mine and it works perfectly. I use a small hand-grinder on my favorite locally freshly-roasted coffee beans (just enough for a single cup) then spoon the fresh ground coffee into the stainless steel filter resting over my coffee cup, place it under my Keurig and choose the hot water setting. PERFECT and FAST.

A couple personal notes regarding some reviews that talked about the filter letting grounds slip through, weak coffee, and the lack of mugs included:
1. I used a medium-fine grind and the filter didn't let anything through, so perhaps they used a super-fine grind?
2. I like strong coffee and I didn't a problem with the brew strength. Perhaps they didn't use enough coffee? I also used the 4 oz. hot water portion and ran it twice to get a single 8 oz cup of coffee.
3. Regarding the lack of coffee mugs, I personally didn't assume they would be included so I wasn't upset like a couple of the other reviewers were. that said, it might be a good idea for the listing company to expressly state "no mugs included" just to avoid any misunderstandings.

Personally, I loved the product, thought it performed even better than expected, and will absolutely be giving some of these as gifts!
Perfect with my favorite coffee and very transportable when I'm traveling.

In the last 5 years I have had at least 5 Keurig coffee machines.  I get 9 months to 18 months out of them and they break.  Yes I can return them however that is getting old.  The last time I switched and bought the Cuisinart brand and now 12 months later it is broken.  I travel for a living and I'm only home about 13 days a month therefore I expect more out of my name brand coffee makers.  I only use bottled water in my coffee makers, therefore I expect more.  As you can imagine I didn't want to spend a couple of hundred dollars just to get through another year.  I had also just bought a Costco box of Keurig coffee pods.  I misread the description on this and thought I could just drop a pod in and pour hot water.  It doesn't work that way.  I woke this morning in my usual stupid before coffee state.  I realized I couldn't just insert the pod so I just opened it and dumped the grounds into the filter and poured the hot water over it.  I'm now drinking my second cup and it is just as good as the $280.00 Cuisinart. If I have to buy one of these yearly I a still saving $100s every year.  This is easy, simple and much cheaper.  I'd rather buy this every year then ever buy another Keurig machine again.

I have tried all the reusable and use-your-own-coffee K-cups, and didn't like any of them. Either they didn't work right in my machine or the coffee measurement was really hard to figure out to get the right strength of the brew. THESE ARE PERFECT AND SIMPLE. Just use your Keurig machine as a hot water dispenser and have a nice on-demand cup of pour-over coffee. Note that the grind can affect the drip and strength of coffee, but overall I haven't had a cup made from these that isn't good. Highly recommend if you're trying to avoid all the waste generated by K-cups.

The coffee I made this morning with my Keurig was great.  As other reviews have mentioned, no grounds other than very fine particles got through the filter.  One bit of advice:  my coffee cup is 4.25'' in diameter and this fits perfectly.  Wider mugs you may need to do a little balancing.  I tried sitting it on a large mug with a 4.75'' and it just sat on the rim of the cup.  If you were pouring water from a kettle you should use caution that it doesn't tip.  I haven't tried the tea infuser yet but I'm sure it will work as well as the coffee filter.

My primary use for this filter is for camping. I like at least a medium strength brew and use the individual cup filter, have not tried the larger filter for a carafe size brew.

With boiling water it required 7 minutes to achieve a medium strength brew. The coffee was still hot enough to enjoy but if you like to sit down with it while it's still too hot to drink you would probably have to reheat it after brewing. This was in a 68 degree room so if you're brewing in colder temps outside it may not be hot enough at the end of the brew.

On the first cup I made, after taking the last gulp, I was rewarded with not just a little but a significant amount of grounds in my mouth. This was with a premium brand of ground coffee so wasn't expecting the filter to perform that poorly. I'll be using paper filters. Not a big deal if you're camping since it's actually an easier cleanup with paper filters when camping. Just something to be aware of.

These are rather cheesy I'm afraid.  One of the knobs was molded with a divot on one side so the metal indicator plate won't seat down all the way. Then after putting the knobs on, they don't fit snugly on the adaptors and tend to fall off when you touch them....so I got out the Shoo Goo and glopped up the adaptors in the hope the knobs would stay.  So far that hack is working.  They don't look too bad once they're on there it's just getting them to function that's the problem.  On the good side, the metal plates can be rotated around the face of the knobs to indicate where you want the "off" to be, and the oven knob has 2 temperature plates which are both different (depending on which way your oven knob turns).

Been using this filter for a couple of days now and there are a few reasons why it deserves 5 stars.
I have tested it brewing regular, even though I almost always brew inverted, just to see how well it held the water without letting it seep too fast. For a metal filter it’s pretty darn close to paper when it comes to that.
It’s very easy to clean as it is one solid piece of metal with perforated holes. This also makes me feel very comfortable about its durability.
It doesn't let fine grinds into my cup of coffee. I haven't tested it yet with a super fine grind like espresso or Turkish and to be honest I probably won’t. I like a coarser grind and this filter is perfect for grit free coffee.

At first I thought this filter would be great. And don't get me wrong, it works fine. The only problem I have with it is that it seems to let some of the fine sediment come through and I started immediately noticing a different taste to my coffee. I only use Dunkin' Donuts Regular Blend ground coffee. And when I first got my AeroPress over a year ago I was amazed at how MUCH better the coffee tasted than from my old 4 cup percolator.
So when I started running low on paper filters last month I ordered the Disc. I played around a little with how much coffee to put in after switching over but I kept getting a different taste and noticing the fine sludge in my cup.
Maybe the coarseness should be adjusted but I feel like it won't make much of a difference. And I might play with it at some point but now I'm using the paper filters again and will probably order some more. If I was traveling and bringing my AeroPress I would probably pack the Disk, but for everyday use I'm sticking with the paper filters.
Very fast shipping and works as promised. My coffee tastes great (I make 2-3 cups a day) and no more worrying about ordering paper filters. I love.
